newsitem.title: JAPAN: FORECAST-Japan 97/98 growth seen more than 2 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Japan 97/98 growth seen more than 2 pct.

text.p: Japan's gross domestic product (GDP) is likely to grow more than two percent in real terms in the next fiscal year from April 1, 1997, a private research institute said on Monday.

The Research Institute on the National Economy forecast in a report that Japan's official discount rate, now at an all-time low of 0.5 percent, would be raised by 0.5 percentage point to one percent next fiscal year.
Many other private economic institutions have predicted real growth of less than two percent for 1997/98 after an estimated 2.5 percent growth in the current fiscal year.
The report said economic growth in 1997/98 would be led by private demand, while public demand and exports were likely to be neutral towards overall growth.

The expected increase in the official discount rate would not signal a credit tightening by the Bank of Japan and the central bank's monetary policy would continue to be conducted in such a way as to support economic expansion, it added.

The report said the growth forecast was based on the assumption that 1996's special income tax cut would not be implemented in 1997, and that Japan's sales tax would be raised to five percent from three percent on April 1 as scheduled.
